land.text: the Emirate of Córdoba of Abd al-Rahman III, without Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March still outside his rule

predecessors.note: One state under a new title: 'From 756 it was ruled as an independent emirate until Abd al-Rahman III proclaimed himself as caliph in 929'. Cliopatria keeps two rows (Emirate to 935, Caliphate from 936) with different Wikidata ids; the emirate dossier ends in January 929.

land.text: Córdoba and its vicinity, the republic of Abu 'l-Hazm Jahwar from 1031

successors.note: Hisham III was deposed on 30 November 1031. The other taifas had split off earlier, 1009-1028 (see the loss events). Cliopatria's Caliphate row keeps this Córdoba shape to 1071; it is the Taifa of Córdoba (to 1070, then Seville), not the Caliphate.

capitals.name: Córdoba (Qurṭuba)
capitals.note: The page names Córdoba as the capital and Madinat al-Zahra as the caliphs' palace-city (a mint there c. 947); it dates no move of the seat, so one entry.

rulers.name: Abd al-Rahman III
rulers.title: caliph (emir from 912)
rulers.note: Declared himself caliph 16 January 929 (infobox 17 January); 'He died on 15 October 961'.

rulers.name: Al-Hakam II
rulers.note: 'succeeded by his 46-year-old son, Al-Hakam II, in 961'; 'The death of the caliph in 976' (Almanzor page).

rulers.name: Hisham II
rulers.note: 'invested as caliph on or about Monday, 1 October 976' (Almanzor page); the chamberlain Almanzor (d. 8 August 1002) and his sons held the power. The end of the reign is not given on the pages opened; 1008 is the year before the Fitna began ('a coup d'état' in 1009).

rulers.name: Rival caliphs of the Fitna of al-Andalus
rulers.title: contending caliphs
rulers.note: Dated on the Fitna page: Hisham II's Amirid supporters killed one caliph on 23 July 1010; Yahya was proclaimed on 13 August 1021; al-Qasim was deposed on 10 September 1023; another caliph was deposed on 26 May 1025; allegiance was pledged on 15 June 1026. The pages opened do not give a complete list of the caliphs, so the strip names the period.

rulers.name: Hisham III
rulers.note: 'The last Córdoban Caliph was Hisham III, who reigned from 1027 to 1031'; 'deposed ... in 30 November 1031'.

New keyframe, 930-931: Badajoz is back ('the surrender of Ibn Marwan of Badajoz in 930'); Toledo and the Upper March are still out.

The page's Zaragoza campaign is 937, so the shape holds for 937-939; at Simancas (939) 'the Christian forces ... crush the caliphal army' and the kingdom-of-leon dossier (from its Ramiro II page) has the Leonese border moving from the Duero to the Tormes, so from 940 the 947 shape applies. Area against the page: 'some four hundred thousand square kilometers' around 1000, but the 936 shape is 408k: ratio 1.02, consistent. Ceuta added (the Cliopatria shape ends at 36.03 N; Ceuta is 35.89 N).

correction.text: the 947 shape, holding from 940 (not 947) to 950: al-Andalus without the Duero-Tormes belt that Ramiro II took after 939, plus Ceuta: 'The caliph helped the Maghrawa Berbers conquer Melilla (927), Ceuta (931) and Tangiers (951)'

The cause is the Leonese advance after Simancas (939), which the kingdom-of-leon dossier's Ramiro II page puts after that victory without a year; the ledger dates the loss to 939 and this shape applies from 940 to 950, with Ceuta added; Tangier follows in the 951 keyframe.

correction.text: the 947 shape plus Ceuta and Tangier: 'The caliph helped the Maghrawa Berbers conquer Melilla (927), Ceuta (931) and Tangiers (951)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 951-960: Tangier joins Ceuta ('Tangiers (951)'). Cliopatria's 947 shape (358,866 km2) ends at 36.03 N, south of both. After the Fatimid offensive of 958 'abd al-Rahman kept only the strongholds of Ceuta and Tangiers', so both stay to 961. Northern Morocco in 949-958 is a client tint in the ledger, not part of this shape.

358,817 km2: the same Iberian shape, 961-965 after the correction. The page has Abd al-Rahman III's death on 15 October 961 and Al-Hakam II's accession, and that caliphal influence in the Maghreb 'disappeared after a Fatimid offensive in 958' while he 'kept only the strongholds of Ceuta and Tangiers'; Cliopatria's shape has no Africa at all, so Ceuta and Tangier are added (reviewer finding, repaired 2026-10-25).

The page says only that 'much of northern Morocco also came directly within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate' and that the Idrisids were beaten in 973-974 (Almanzor page); nothing on the pages gives direct rule there, and nothing at all for western Algeria. Corrected to the Iberian shape plus Ceuta, Tangier and Calahorra, with the African part a vassal tint (ledger 974-1015). Without Africa the shape is 358,110 km2.

keyframe_review.note: 564,714 km2 with Africa; 369,491 km2 without it, against the page's 'some four hundred thousand square kilometers' around 1000 CE (ratio 0.92 without Africa, 1.41 with). Same correction as 980. The shape is 11,512 km2 larger than the 980 shape because of the Mondego (Coimbra, Aveiro) taken from León: ledger 990, confidence 1 (the Caliphate page: Coimbra 'recovered in the 980s').

keyframe_review.note: 345,718 km2 for 1010-1014, 574 of its 1,310 cells in Morocco and Algeria. The Fitna began in 1009 and the first taifas arose 1009-1013 (Taifa page), so Cliopatria's shape is the starting state for 1010 only; the loss events of 1011-1013 (Murcia, Almería, Arcos, Albarracín, Saltés and Huelva, Granada, Carmona, Morón) carve it down to the 1015 shape. Africa removed as in 980.

70,873 km2 for 1015-1017: Córdoba, Seville and the Algarve coast, Málaga, and still the Upper March around Zaragoza (the Taifa page dates Zaragoza's taifa to 1018). The Balearic Islands have left (ledger 1015, conf 1). Adjusted: Ceuta and Tangier stay (Hammudid governors, May 1013, Hammudid page) until the 1026 loss, and Calahorra (966) until the 1018 Zaragoza loss.

correction.text: 1018 shape without the Taifa of Seville (from 1023), plus Ceuta and Tangier to 1025

keyframe_review.note: 34,890 km2 for 1018-1027. The shape holds Seville, Huelva and Málaga to 1027, but the Taifa page gives 'Seville: 1023-1091' and 'Málaga: 1026-1057/1058', so the shape is correct for 1018-1022 and from 1023 loses the Seville shape of 1028. Ceuta and Tangier are added until Málaga becomes a taifa in 1026 (ledger 1026, confidence 1); Calahorra has gone with the Upper March in 1018.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, holding to 30 November 1031

keyframe_review.note: 15,032 km2: Córdoba and the Beja strip. Correct to 31 (30 November 1031: 'so they deposed Hisham III in 30 November 1031'); the Caliphate ends there, not in 1033 or 1071. The Taifa of Mértola page (opened 2026-10-25) has the taifa 1033-1044 with 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1033', capital Mértola, under Seville's Abbad II; it does not mention Beja. The strip therefore left the Córdoba rump in 1033 (Cliopatria's year), two years after the Caliphate itself.

correction.text: the same shape, to be drawn as the Taifa of Córdoba (the Jahwarid republic) 1031-1069, not as the Caliphate

keyframe_review.note: 9,813 km2, 1034-1065: Córdoba and its vicinity, which from 1031 is the Taifa of Córdoba: 'replaced the Umayyad Caliph as the government of Córdoba and its vicinity in 1031'; 'Abu 'l-Hazm led Córdoba from 1031 until his death in 1043'. Not the Caliphate, which ended in 1031. The taifa-of-cordoba dossier (another group) should take this shape.

correction.text: the same shape: Taifa of Córdoba to 1069, from 1070 held by the Taifa of Seville

keyframe_review.note: 9,788 km2, 1066-1071: still Córdoba. 'In 1070, after defeating the Toledan army, al-Mu'tamid captured Córdoba' (Seville annexes it); the page adds that Seville lost control of Córdoba from 1075 to 1078 and held it to 1091.

region.text: al-Andalus without Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March

ledger.note: 929: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims the Caliphate of Córdoba. 'declare himself Caliph of Córdoba on 16 January 929' (the infobox says 17 January); the Caliphate page: 'From 756 it was ruled as an independent emirate until Abd al-Rahman III proclaimed himself as caliph in 929'. Same state under a new title (rule 2); the page names 'most of the Iberian Peninsula' as its territory, not a boundary, so the region is the Emirate's shape without the cities the page dates later.
930: Badajoz submits. 'the surrender of Ibn Marwan of Badajoz in 930.' Badajoz later becomes a taifa in 1009.

ledger.counterpart: Ceuta's previous holders (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 931: Ceuta is secured against the Fatimids. 'Fatimid invasions were thwarted when Abd al-Rahman III secured Melilla in 927, Ceuta in 931, and Tangier in 951'; the Abd al-Rahman III page: 'The Maghrawa Berbers, backed by Abd al-Rahman, conquered Ceuta in 931'. Neither page names who held Ceuta before, so the counterpart is a description; the year is the page's, the extent of the claim is not.

By 931: Nekor is the caliph's client (mirror of emirate-of-nekor /ledger/4). Nekor page (opened 2026-10-25): 'In 927 he began his policy of defensive expansion by occupying Melilla'; 'Musa ibn Abi'l-Afiya attacked and vanquished the Umayyad's vassal, al-Mu'ayyad, the Salihid ruler of Nekor' and his troops 'besieged, sacked, and burned Nekor in 931'. The page gives no start or end for the allegiance to Córdoba; 931 is the year the vassal is attested, and the real start may lie in 927-929.

region.text: Toledo surrenders after a two-year siege

ledger.note: 932: Toledo surrenders after a two-year siege. 'The city surrendered on 2 August 932, after a siege of two years.'

region.text: Nekor, sacked by the Fatimids in 934

ledger.note: 934: bridge (mirror of emirate-of-nekor /ledger/7). Nekor page: 'Fatimid troops sacked the city twice, in 917 and in 934'; it does not say when the allegiance to Córdoba ended, so 934, the next dated event, is a bridge.

region.text: the Upper March: Zaragoza, Huesca and Lérida

ledger.counterpart: Muhammad ibn Hashim al-Tugib, governor of Zaragoza
ledger.note: 937: the Upper March returns. The page has the governor of Zaragoza 'who had allied with Ramiro but was pardoned after the capture of his city' in the 937 campaign (the year is the page's reading of the campaign, the three provinces are mine).

937: war on the Leonese frontier. 'In 937 Abd al-Rahman conquered some thirty castles in León'; the caliphal army is crushed at Simancas in 939 and a peace is signed with León in 951. The zone is the belt the Leonese border moved across.

region.text: the land between the Duero and the Tormes

ledger.note: 939: the Duero-Tormes belt is lost at Simancas. 'crush the caliphal army in 939 at the Battle of Simancas.' The kingdom-of-leon dossier, from its Ramiro II page, has the victory 'allowed the advance of the Leonese border of the Duero to the Tormes'; it gives no year for the advance and Cliopatria draws it from 947.

region.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

ledger.note: 949: northern Morocco is occupied and becomes a client of the caliph. Caliphate page: 'In 948, the Idrisid emir Abul-Aish Ahmad recognized the caliphate, but refused to allow them to occupy Tangier. The Umayyads besieged Tangier in 949 and defeated Abul-Aish, forcing him to retreat ... and then occupied the rest of northern Morocco.' Idrisid page (second page): Abul-'Aysh, ruling 948-954, kept 'only the areas around al-Basra and Asilah while the Umayyads occupied the rest of northern Morocco'. Drawn as a client tint, not as annexation: the Abd al-Rahman III page calls it 'a protectorate covering the northern and central Maghreb, supporting the Idrisid dynasty'. Mirror of fatimid-caliphate /ledger/20 (948 loss, confidence 2, whose region is Morocco outside the Rif and Jbala); the page's year is 949 for the siege, 948 for the recognition. The region is the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape, a reading of the page's 'northern Morocco'.

951: peace with León. 'In 951 he signed a peace with the new king of León.' (Ordoño III; the same page puts Ordoño III's defeat in 956 and homage of Sancho, García Sánchez and Queen Toda at Córdoba in 958.)

951: Tangier is taken from the Idrisids. 'In 948, the Idrisid emir Abul-Aish Ahmad recognized the caliphate, but refused to allow them to occupy Tangier. The Umayyads besieged Tangier in 949 and defeated Abul-Aish'; 'secured ... Tangier in 951'.

region.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

ledger.note: 958: the Fatimid offensive ends the caliph's influence. Abd al-Rahman III page: 'the Caliphate's influence in the area disappeared after a Fatimid offensive in 958' and 'abd al-Rahman kept only the strongholds of Ceuta and Tangiers' (both stay in the shapes). Caliphate page: 'Another Fatimid invasion of Morocco occurred in 958, led by the general, Jawhar'; Idrisid page: 'In 958 the Fatimids sent a new general, Jawhar' and the Idrisids 'again accept Fatimid overlordship'. The Idrisid page adds that the Umayyads 'made a comeback' once the Fatimids were busy with Egypt, undated, so nothing is drawn between 959 and the 973 campaign. The fatimid-caliphate dossier should record the 958 recovery of this land (its /ledger/21 covers only the Rif and Jbala).

region.text: Calahorra and the valley of the River Cidacos

ledger.note: 966: Calahorra is taken. Kingdom of Navarre page (opened 2026-10-25): 'In 966, clashes between the Caliphate of Córdoba and the kingdom resulted in the loss of Calahorra and the valley of the River Cidacos.' Mirror of kingdom-of-pamplona /ledger/6. Cliopatria's Caliphate shapes do not reach Calahorra (0 cells in 961 and 980), so the keyframes from 966 add the circle; the same page has 'the city of Calahorra was wrested from the Moors' in 1045 (kingdom-of-pamplona /ledger/25 names taifa-of-zaragoza), so the 1018 Zaragoza loss carries it.

region.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

ledger.note: 973: the caliphal campaign against the Idrisids. 'In 973, he undertook the logistical, administrative and diplomatic aspects of the caliphal campaign' (Almanzor, then Ibn Abi Amir). The page names no land ('the Maghreb', 'North Africa'); the zone is the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape, read from the Caliphate page's northern Morocco, and Algeria is no longer included.

region.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

ledger.note: 974: northern Morocco comes under the caliph's sway. 'By 974, Al-Hassan II was taken to Córdoba, and the remaining Idrisids recognized Umayyad rule'; 'In the 10th century, much of northern Morocco also came directly within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate.' Drawn as a lighter tint: the pages give no garrisons or governors. The region is the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape only (it runs south to 31.4 N); nothing opened supports western Algeria, which Cliopatria also draws from 980. The year is the end of the Idrisid campaign.

region.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

ledger.note: 974: victory over the Idrisids. 'Achieving victory against the Idrisids, Ibn Abi Amir returned sick to the Cordoban court in September 974.'

region.text: the Mondego, the Beira and the Duero edge that León held in 989 and not in 990

ledger.note: 990: the Mondego (Coimbra, Aveiro) passes to the Caliphate (bridge, confidence 1; mirror of kingdom-of-leon /ledger/7). Cliopatria's 990 shape is 11,512 km2 larger than its 980 shape (553,202 to 564,713 km2, the African part unchanged) and Leon's 961 shape loses 11,400 km2 in 990. The Caliphate page says the new Atlantic base at Alcácer do Sal 'protected the city of Coimbra, recovered in the 980s' (no year, no ruler); the Almanzor page, reopened 2026-10-25, does not mention Coimbra or the Mondego. The year is Cliopatria's shape year, the page gives only the decade.
1009: Alpuente breaks away. 'Alpuente: 1009-1106 (to Almoravids)'. The Fitna page: it 'began in the year 1009 with a coup d'état'.

1009: Badajoz breaks away. Taifa of Badajoz page (opened 2026-10-25): 'Sabur al-Saqlabi 1009-1022' in the ruler list and, in the infobox, 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1009'; the page gives no 'established' year of its own. The year is the page's; the region is Cliopatria's 1010 shape. The Badajoz dossier also founds the taifa in 1009.

1010: Toledo breaks away (bridge, confidence 1). The Taifa page has no dated entry for Toledo and Cliopatria starts the taifa in 1010. The Taifa of Toledo page (opened 2026-10-25) disagrees: 'Established: 1018 (de facto)', when Ismail 'expelled Toledo's governor', and 'Already by 1036, Ismail al-Zahir appears as sovereign king'. Kept at 1010 because Cliopatria's Caliphate 1015 shape has no Toledo and its Toledo row begins in 1010; the taifa-of-toledo dossier should settle 1010 or 1018.

1010: Tortosa breaks away. Taifa of Tortosa page (opened 2026-10-25): the taifa 'existed for two separate periods, from 1010 to 1060 and 1081 to 1099', infobox 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1010', founded by 'Labib al-Fata al-Saqlabi'. The year is the page's; the region is Cliopatria's 1010 shape (the earlier note that the Taifa page dates Tortosa from 1039 was a different table).
1010: Valencia breaks away. 'Valencia: 1010/1011-1094 (to El Cid, nominally vassal of Castile but allied to Banu Hud)'.
1010: Dénia breaks away. 'Denia: 1010/1012-1076 (to Zaragoza)'.
1011: Murcia breaks away. 'Murcia: 1011/1012-1065 (to Valencia)'.
1011: Almería breaks away. 'Almería: 1011-1091 (to Almoravids)'. No Cliopatria row, so the region is the province.
1011: Albarracín breaks away. 'Albarracín: 1011-1104 (to Almoravids)'.
1011: Arcos breaks away. 'Arcos: 1011-1068 (to Seville)'.
1012: Saltés and Huelva breaks away. 'Saltés and Huelva: 1012/1013-1051/1053 (Bakrid Dynasty)'.
1013: Granada breaks away. 'Granada: 1013-1090 (to Almoravids)'.
1013: Carmona breaks away. 'Carmona: 1013-1091 (to Seville)'.
1013: Morón breaks away. 'Morón: 1013-1066 (to Seville)'.

1015: the Balearic Islands leave. The Taifa page dates the independent taifa of Majorca to 1018 ('Majorca: 1018-1203 (to Almohads)'); Cliopatria's shape drops the islands in 1015 and the Dénia dossier has Mujahid's fleet take them in 1015 from its own page. A bridge, not a dated event of this page.

region.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

ledger.note: 1015: the Moroccan clients are gone. Cliopatria drops Morocco and Algeria from the shape in 1015; neither the Caliphate page nor the Fitna page says when the sphere of influence ended, so this is a bridge over the Fitna. The Hammudid page (opened 2026-10-25) is silent on Morocco; it dates only the governorships of Ceuta, Tangier and Algeciras (May 1013).

union.text: Calahorra, held since 966, goes with the Upper March (reading)

region.text: the Upper March: Zaragoza, Huesca and Lérida; with Calahorra and the Cidacos valley, gained in 966

ledger.note: 1018: Zaragoza becomes a taifa. 'Zaragoza: 1018-1046 (to Banu Tujib; then to Banu Hud)'. Calahorra (gained 966) is read as passing to Zaragoza with the Upper March: the Navarre page has 'the city of Calahorra was wrested from the Moors' in 1045 and the kingdom-of-pamplona dossier names taifa-of-zaragoza as the loser; no page opened here dates the transfer, so the region part is a reading.
1023: Seville breaks away. 'Seville: 1023-1091 (to Almoravids)'; 'Niebla: 1023/1024-1091 (to Seville)'. Cliopatria dates the Seville shape from 1028.
1023: Niebla breaks away. 'Niebla: 1023/1024-1091 (to Seville)'.
1026: Málaga becomes a taifa. 'Málaga: 1026-1057/1058 (to Granada); 1073-1090 (to Almoravids)'. No Cliopatria row exists for it, so the region is the province.

region.text: Ceuta and Tangier, the Hammudid governorships of 1013, with Málaga's taifa

ledger.note: 1026: Ceuta and Tangier leave with the Hammudid taifa of Málaga (bridge, confidence 1). Hammudid page (opened 2026-10-25), Encyclopaedia of Islam footnote: Sulayman al-Musta'in (Shawwal 403 AH, May 1013) 'allotted to 'Ali b. Hammud the governorship of Ceuta and to his brother al-Kasim that of Algeciras, Tangier, and Arzila'; the Hammudids ruled Málaga until the Zirids of Granada took it in 1056, 'They were then forced to settle in Ceuta', and its table gives a Ceuta taifa 1009-1055 (which contradicts the footnote). The Hammudids were themselves caliphs of Córdoba 1016-1023 and 1025-1027, so Ceuta and Tangier are read as inside the rump until Málaga becomes a taifa in 1026. The taifa-of-ceuta dossier founds in 1061 from taifa-of-malaga.

region.text: what was left in 1031: Córdoba and its vicinity

ledger.note: 1031: the Caliphate is abolished. 'The Fitna finally ended with the definitive abolition of the Caliphate of Córdoba in 1031' and 'they deposed Hisham III in 30 November 1031'; Córdoba becomes a republic under Abu 'l-Hazm Jahwar (Taifa of Córdoba page). Only Córdoba and its vicinity were left.

wars.name: Leonese wars of Abd al-Rahman III (Simancas)
wars.outcome: Caliphal army crushed at Simancas in 939; Leon's border moves from the Duero to the Tormes; peace with the new king of León in 951.
wars.note: 'In 937 Abd al-Rahman conquered some thirty castles in León'; 956: 'the defeat of Ramiro's successor, Ordoño III of León'; 958: Sancho, García Sánchez and Queen Toda 'all paid homage to Abd al-Rahman in Córdoba'; 959-960: help to retake Zamora and Oviedo and overthrow Ordoño IV. The homage is not drawn as vassalage: the page gives no land, tribute or duration.

wars.name: Abd al-Rahman III's Maghreb campaigns against the Fatimids and Idrisids

zones.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

wars.outcome: Melilla (927), Ceuta (931) and Tangier (951) secured; northern Morocco occupied from 949 as a client area (ledger 949) and lost with the Fatimid offensive of 958, after which 'abd al-Rahman kept only the strongholds of Ceuta and Tangiers'.
wars.note: 949: 'The Umayyads besieged Tangier in 949 and defeated Abul-Aish ... and then occupied the rest of northern Morocco' (Caliphate page); 958: 'Another Fatimid invasion of Morocco occurred in 958, led by the general, Jawhar'. Melilla is not drawn: see the dossier notes.

wars.name: Almanzor's Idrisid campaign

zones.text: the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape ('much of northern Morocco ... within the sphere of influence of the Córdoban Caliphate'); Morocco only, no page names Algeria

wars.outcome: Victory over the Idrisids: 'By 974, Al-Hassan II was taken to Córdoba, and the remaining Idrisids recognized Umayyad rule' (Caliphate page); northern Morocco is a client tint 974-1015.
wars.note: Almanzor page: the campaign was run by Ibn Abi Amir as High Qadi of the Umayyad possessions in North Africa, 973-September 974. In September 979 he 'sent troops from Algeciras to the aid of Ceuta', 'threatened by the victorious campaign of Buluggin ibn Ziri, supported by the Fatimids, against Umayyad clients in the Western Maghreb'. The page names no land taken, so the relief of Ceuta is no ledger event (Ceuta was already the Caliphate's, ledger 931).

wars.name: Campaigns of Almanzor against the Christian kingdoms

zones.text: the Mondego, the Beira and the Duero edge that León held in 989 and not in 990

wars.outcome: Annual raids: Salamanca, Baños de Ledesma and Cuéllar (977), Atienza (980), Zamora (September 981), Portuguese lands probably Viseu, Pamplona and Barcelona; Almanzor died at Medinaceli on 8 August 1002. The Mondego (Coimbra, Aveiro) is held from the 980s ('recovered in the 980s', Caliphate page), drawn from 990 (Cliopatria's shape year, ledger 990 at confidence 1).
wars.note: 'In 985, the fleet ravaged the Catalans' (Caliphate page). The Almanzor page opened only reached about 990, so the sack of León (988) and Santiago (997) are not on a page read here.

wars.name: Fitna of al-Andalus
wars.outcome: Civil war that ended with the abolition of the Caliphate on 30 November 1031 and the rise of about 33 taifas.
wars.note: 'It began in the year 1009 with a coup d'état'; Yahya entered Córdoba on 13 August 1021; Hammudids were repelled from Córdoba on 11 May 1026.

certainty.note: The Caliphate's frontiers with León, Castile, Pamplona and the Catalan counties were marches with castles and raids, never surveyed; the African clients are a sphere of influence. No border in the life is treaty-fixed on the pages opened (the 951 peace with León sets none).

notes: Cliopatria rows: (1) the Caliphate row runs 936-1071 but the Caliphate ended on 30 November 1031; the 1034 and 1066 shapes (Córdoba only) are the Taifa of Córdoba and then Seville and are marked wrong. (2) 929-935 is missing from the Caliphate row (it sits in the Emirate row's 926-935 shape, which holds Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March before the page dates them); three new keyframes (929, 930, 932) carve it. The emirate-of-cordoba dossier already ends in January 929 and names this state as its successor. (3) The 980, 990 and 1010 shapes draw Morocco and western Algeria as direct territory (the largest, 564,714 km2); the pages support only a sphere of influence over northern Morocco, so they are corrected to a vassal tint (974-1015) and nothing supports western Algeria. (4) The Duero-Tormes belt: the 936 shape holds it to 946 and Leon's shape takes it in 947; the page-based year is 939 (Simancas), the shape change is Cliopatria's 947; the keyframe verdicts shift the years only. (5) Taifa dates come from the Taifa page and differ by a year or two from Cliopatria's (Alpuente 1009, Granada 1013, Seville 1023 vs 1028); the Cliopatria taifa shapes are used as the regions. Badajoz, Toledo and Tortosa have no dated entry on that page: conf 1. (6) The Taifa page has Málaga (1026-1057/1058, 1073-1090) and Almería (1011-1091) as taifas; Cliopatria has no row for either (Almería is on the group's list as taifa-of-almeria; Málaga is not): counterparts_needing_dossiers. (7) The Caliphate page at the accented URL was a restructuring banner; the unaccented URL returned the article under the title 'Umayyad state of Córdoba' (the emirate and caliphate in one article), so the infobox fields were not labelled and the infobox area is the body's 'some four hundred thousand square kilometers' around 1000 CE. (8) Not dated by any page opened: the year Morocco's clients fell away (bridge 1015), the exact end of Ceuta and Tangier (read as 1026 with Málaga, confidence 1), the Beja part of the strip in the 1018-1033 shapes (the Mértola page dates the taifa 1033 and does not mention Beja), and whether Almanzor's Barcelona raid (c. 978-980 on the page) was 985. (9) Page budget: five pages plus the Taifa article. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-25 after the adversarial review: (a) Ceuta (931) and Tangier (951) are now in every keyframe from 932 to 1025 (new keyframes 951 and 966; 961 and 1015 became adjust; the 947 verdict now covers 940-950) and leave with Málaga's taifa in 1026 (Hammudid page, confidence 1). (b) Northern Morocco is a client tint 949-958 (ledger vassal_start/vassal_end, counterpart idrisids, confidence 2) and again 974-1015, always as the Moroccan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape; Algeria is dropped everywhere. The 980 shape runs south to 31.4 N, further than 'northern Morocco'. (c) The 979 Ceuta occupation pair is deleted: the relief of Ceuta changes nothing on the map. (d) Mirrors added: emirate-of-nekor 931/934 vassal pair, kingdom-of-pamplona 966 gain (Calahorra, carried to the 1018 Zaragoza loss), kingdom-of-leon 990 gain (the Mondego). (e) Badajoz loss moved to 1009 and Tortosa raised to confidence 2 on the Taifa of Badajoz and Taifa of Tortosa pages; Toledo stays 1010 at confidence 1 although the Taifa of Toledo page has 'Established: 1018 (de facto)'. (f) Melilla (occupied 927 per the Nekor page; 'kept only Ceuta and Tangiers' after 958) is NOT drawn: it is a point-sized town on the edge of Nekor's shape (Cliopatria's Nekor 926 shape ends at 35.22 N, the gazetteer's Melilla cell is at 35.23 N, 0 cells in common), no page dates its loss, and drawing it would need a confidence-1 loss for one grid cell. (g) The 1010 keyframe keeps Murcia and Almería; the 1011 events remove them. Disagreements: the idrisids dossier ends in 974 with a loss and a dissolve into this state, while this dossier keeps a client tint of 'idrisids' to 1015 because the pages say 'sphere of influence' and 'remaining Idrisids recognized Umayyad rule'; fatimid-caliphate /ledger/20 dates the loss of Morocco 948, the Caliphate page 949 (siege of Tangier); the Hammudid page's table (Ceuta taifa 1009-1055) contradicts its 1013 footnote.
